groupedBar.name: groupedBar
groupedBar.description: Compare every metric column across scenarios at once, grouped by scenario. Doesn't read any props, and "y" here only satisfies the example schema - every column in the data is plotted regardless of its value.

bar.name: bar
bar.description: Compare a single metric across scenarios as vertical or horizontal bars. Supports props: "unit", "color"/"colors".

pie.name: pie
pie.description: Show a single metric's share across scenarios as a pie chart. Supports props: "unit", "color"/"colors".

table.name: table
table.description: List a single metric per scenario in a plain two-column table. Supports props: "unit".

lollipop.name: lollipop
lollipop.description: Compare a single metric across scenarios as a horizontal lollipop chart. Supports props: "unit", "color"/"colors".

GroupedBarVega.name: GroupedBarVega
GroupedBarVega.description: The same grouped-bar comparison, written as a declarative chart spec instead of by hand. Doesn't read any props, and "y" here only satisfies the example schema - every column in the data is plotted regardless of its value.

TraSculptorMatrixD3.name: TraSculptorMatrixD3
TraSculptorMatrixD3.description: TraSculptor Matrix combines a scenario history tree with a road-level comparison matrix to show how transportation network modifications affect traffic conditions across alternative states. Each column represents a network state and its relationship to a parent state, while each row represents an individual road. Within each matrix cell, traffic flow relative to capacity controls glyph width, travel-time efficiency relative to free-flow travel time controls glyph height, and the background indicates whether travel time improved or worsened compared with the baseline. Scenario-level annotations can also show optimization improvement, modification type, and cumulative cost. Adapted from the visual comparison design in TraSculptor (Deng et al., TVCG 2025).

BNVARouteMatrixD3.name: BNVARouteMatrixD3
BNVARouteMatrixD3.description: A matrix-based comparison of alternative scenarios across multiple performance criteria, adapted from BNVA (Weng et al., TVCG 2021). Each row represents an alternative scenario and each column represents a criterion. Horizontal bars encode the relative value of each criterion, while distributions in the column headers summarize values across all alternatives. Dashed reference markers indicate the baseline scenario, making it easy to assess trade-offs, rank alternatives, and compare candidate scenarios against the original configuration.
